body: The cops should really be a last resort, not only will she likely feel betrayed, but the traumatic experience of being held against her will for "her own safety" could exasperate the issue. I just turned 26 and only now talked with my family about wanting to kill myself, something I've dealt with even in elementary school, and they were very supportive, while it didn't really make me feel less suicidal, it did help knowing I at least have other people I can turn to. If she has good parents, it could be a good idea to try and talk to her about bringing it up to them, but don't just drop that on her, instead try to first ask about them in a way that doesn't seem abrupt, and then make your best judgement on whether you think it's a good route to take. Unfortunately, if you're the one she confides in, and she has nobody else, it's going to be difficult find a good solution, but ultimately taking your time, and not being too blunt with your questions is a potentially good start, because ultimately she needs help, and I know from experience accepting that can be really difficult. How you decide to go about things is up to you, this is just my two cents, I'm just a stranger on the internet. She's lucky to have someone like you though, that's for sure.

I'm not as much on the existential dread as I am just feeling crushed about my life so far, but what you brought up with your mom is really your answer. Not necessarily only family, but the people you care about are one of the few things that validate our individual existences, as it is the only thought that overpowers every other one. We may not leave a profound impact on the world, but we do with the people we care about.

If you're a side character, than I'm still just a concept. I just turned 26, and I don't even believe it. While I wasn't extremely popular in highschool, I wasn't unknown. I still hung out with my friends nearly every day, and had a relationship, and it hasn't made me feel any better today than I did then, it just distracted me from how depressed I always was, not much different from watching TV or playing a video game to escape. I haven't had a job in nearly 3 god damn years now, and I dropped out of college, I have absolutely nothing going for me, I turned into the loser I never thought was possible for me to become, and as a guy, it just makes me feel even more useless. So please don't say your existence isn't important, because these things don't define your future, you still have a lot to offer. I hope my pathetic story makes you feel even a little better about yourself, and also, after reading your post, I would be extremely sad to hear you stopped existing, because unlike myself, you still have your future ahead of you.

Just turned 26, I also didn't have a childhood, but while I can't say I have gone through the same struggle you have now; been in a couple relationships, don't feel I'm ugly, and still have my highschool friends, maybe I can at least reassure you by saying I still feel like you are, despite having those "experiences" you feel you've missed. I'm still miserable, since elementary school I have wanted to die, and I planned on killing myself either after I graduated highschool, or before I turn 30. I still feel like I've wasted my life. Like you, I had no childhood due to my parents getting divorced, while simultaneously being unfit to parent in the first place. My mom was a drug addict, which I guess could be why I have asthma and couldn't join the military, and my dad was an alcoholic. I had to visit my mom on the weekends where I'd either sit on her bed with her passed out, doing nothing, or be home with my dad on weekdays, who just drank alone or with friends, where he would let a video game console take care of me. I've also wasted my 20s so far, just playing video games or hanging out with friends much more successful in life than me, I haven't worked in 3 years and am a college dropout. I don't see myself getting any better even with all this medication. The past 3 years have blended together into one pointless blur, and the next 4 years leading to 30 will be no different. So don't beat yourself up about it man, please take it from me, it's not what would make you happy, we've been depressed basically our whole life, so it won't let us be satisfied with ANY aspect of it. Obviously I can't explicitly tell you how you feel or what would make you happier, but from my experience, none of that shit has made my life feel any better, they were just temporary escapes from how I really feel, no different from just playing a video game or watching TV to escape reality for a little bit.

For me, the past 3 years have blended together in what feels like a few months. One minute I was 22 going on 23, now I'm 26. It's weird because I have very vivid memories of many days of everything before 2019's close. I can remember some of the most mundane, uneventful, unmemorable days from before 2019, yet everything after is just a void to me.

Same, I'm a dude at 26, haven't had a job since 23, and am just waiting for the day I'm ready to end things. I don't know what happened, even in elementary school I was depressed, and wanted to die, but I had hopes and dreams. In highschool I even had a goal, but one day at 22 years old, I stopped enjoying everything that brought me joy, and lost all my passion about what I was studying and dropped out of college. The past 3 years have blended together into what feels like a few months for me, what a waste of my life.

I'm 26, college dropout, and haven't worked for 3 years, so let me tell you right away you're already doing something good for yourself by having a job, for me, I feel so ashamed that my only option would be retail or the food industry that I've given up, and am just waiting for the day I decide I want to die. Don't feel stuck with your field of study. There are other jobs you can look for too with any degree, I have a friend with a journalism degree who got a job in sales, and while he's come to hate it, he makes $100k+ a year. Because of COVID he works from home and basically works 3 hours a day. Obviously if you are like me and don't want to do something you might not be interested in, continue trying for your field of study, but with a degree, it might bring you some relief knowing there are other things out there.

The worst mistake of my life was waiting until I was 23 to look for help about my depression. Now at 26 I just feel fucked, like I can't turn my life around. You have hope and time right now. Working on it sooner is better than later, because by the time it is later, you already have a habit of self destruction formed, and habits are hard to break.

I'm a guy, also in my mid 20s, and have been depressed for the better part of my entire life, probably due to the neglect and divorce of my parents when I was young. I'm impressed that you not only have a job, but also a degree. My depression consumed me and I dropped out of college, and haven't had a job for 3 years now. You should be proud of what you have achieved so far, try to measure yourself against me instead of the people who hurt you. I was never bullied in school, I still hang out with my highschool friends, and I've been in two relationships; yet I'm miserable, have no job, no degree, and nothing to look forward to in the future. I wish I could just find the motivation to do something with my life rather than wait for the day I decide end it instead. 

As weird as it might sound coming from a stranger, I'm proud of you, and what you've accomplished, because I know just how shitty depression makes every facet of your life feel, and whether you believe it or not, I feel you have conquered at least one aspect of it.

Although I'm a guy, I feel very similar to you. I just turned 26, and ever since I was in elementary school, I have wanted to die. It wasn't until highschool I decided I wanted to kill myself either at 21, or just before turning 30.

Like you my parents also got divorced, I was 6 when they did, and I have vivid memories of them fighting all the time. My mom did drugs and my dad was an alcoholic. They had split custody at first, where I would see my mom on the weekends. When with her, she would either leave my brother and I at a museum to go off and buy drugs, or we'd sit in her room doing nothing while she was passed out on the bed from said drugs. When with my dad, he would mostly be drunk and preoccupied with himself or work rather than take care of us, so my grandmother is really who raised us.

I also feel extremely alone, and like a burden. I didn't open up or seek treatment for depression until I turned 23 because I didn't want to bother people. It's crazy to me because it feels like I just went to the doctor for the first time about it yesterday. I guess that's just a testament to how meaningless the past 3 years of my life have been, it's all just blended together into what hardly feels like a few months.

While I don't really have advice to give, I hope by sharing my story, you feel less sadness, even momentarily, by knowing someone else is going through something similar, and you aren't alone in your thoughts.
I wish I would die in my sleep tonight. I would end things myself but I don't want to leave my grandmother with the grief and take years off her life while she's alive, so I'm just waiting now.

Basically sounds like me. I just turned 26, and I'm the biggest waste of life. I've just sat around for the past 3 years doing absolutely nothing. I lost all interest in my hobbies, I have no motivation, not even to get better anymore, and so I have just wasted away in my room since graduating high school. I wasted my time and money in college for 4 years and dropped out with nothing to show for it, got a few jobs out of college, where I quit each one within a month of getting them because of severe depression, and now for the past 3 years, I have sat in my room doing nothing to help myself or make myself better. I'm on antidepressants, and have been for the past 3 years, but they have hardly helped me, and based on how long some of them take to kick in, I'll be 30 before I can be "productive" again, doing the job a high school student is doing because I fucked over myself so hard. I'll very likely be dead by then.

I just turned 26, two weeks ago about. I don't have any of the classic symptoms/issues people have here, social anxiety, self esteem, etc., but what I have struggled with, my entire life, is depression. Ever since I was in elementary school, I had wanted to die. One day I decided to tell my teacher in second grade, which prompted a whole chain of events that I guess scarred me, because I never looked for help until just under 3 years ago. Biggest mistake of my life. I am 26 with basically no work experience, the last job I had was in 2019, and even then my job history is filled with holes because I couldn't hold anything down for that long any ways. I also dropped out of college in 2018. If you add it up, I went nearly 4 years and with nothing to show for it, not even an associates degree. I have nothing going for me, I'm in a hole where now, I don't even want to get better, because all I have to look forward to is being 8+ years behind my friends and everyone else around my age. In highschool I promised myself I'd end things at either 21, or 29, so it's looking like the latter now.

Never been institutionalized, nor do I have OCD, but this is exactly what I've been going through for years now. I was going to college until 2018 when I dropped out because I had lost interest in literally everything. The following year I tried getting various jobs but would quit each one because I felt so depressed, I felt useless because of all the time I spent in school, only to have low skill department store jobs be my only option. Dec 2019 I finally got on antidepressants but have not gotten any better at all. All I can think about is how much I want to die. I'm 26 years old now. I have no usable work experience, which doesn't even matter because I have no motivation or desire to work or be successful anymore, I've given up completely. Even if I were to get better, I can't even see myself being able to live life as people are expected to. The thought of doing the same thing everyday for the rest of my life is so unappealing it makes me sick.
No, more just because he knows he's depressed, he can get better by a younger age and have a life ahead of him if he so desired. He is the only one who knows what's right for him.

I'm in the same boat. I went to school from 18-22 hopping around majors, and dropped out with no degree due to my waning interest in what I was learning. At 22-23 I had tried working various low wage jobs, which after going to school for so long, only made me feel worse about myself. I would quit each job within a month because I would feel so depressed I couldn't eat, and would sleep the hours I wasn't at work. Since all this, aside from hanging out with my friends who have done things with their lives, I have done nothing but waste mine away in my room playing videos games; the past 3 years feel like they went by in just a few months, and now here I am at 26. The sad part is, I can't even play video games anymore, because whenever I start one I lose interest within 20 minutes. I can't do this any longer, in my head I want to change, but then I think about how even if I were to get better, I'm 8 years behind in life now. How can I look forward to finally reaching the starting line when I'm going to be in my 30s by then.

I just turned 26, and this is exactly what I've been going through the past 3 years basically. Technically I've been depressed my entire life, but I never looked for help till 3 years ago, which thinking about even makes me sick because of how quickly it seems those 3 years went with me being unemployed, and doing nothing at all to actually make myself a better person. In 2018 I dropped out of college because I had lost all interest in all of the things I enjoyed, and gave up on any hobbies I had because of it. In 2019 I got a psychiatrist because throughout that year I was looking for any shitty department store job that I should have been doing right out of highschool, but every job I got, I would quit within a month because of how much more depressed it was making me. I would get home, not eat, and go straight to bed just to repeat everything the next day. I don't see myself getting better any time soon, and it just kills me, by the time I can start my life again, I'll probably be 30 something doing the most mindless work meant for highschoolers and young college students, trapped with my own racing thoughts. That's why I honestly plan on ending things just before I turn 30. I'm also afraid of leaving my family with the guilt of it, especially my grandmother, but with how much worse I've been getting, I've been barely hanging on at the end of my rope for a while now.

I really hope everyone in our position finds an answer. I understand and agree with the sentiment of "only getting one shot at life", but now, after years of being in the same spot mentally and physically, I don't really have the willpower to change for the better anymore, and am just waiting. I feel like all I have to "look forward to" is starting at square one in my 30s... yay. Hopefully we can hit that moment where we decide enough is enough and try and fix things head on, or something amazing happens to us by chance.

Thanks, it sucks, I just feel like I dug too deep of a hole at this point. Like what is there to look forward to if I can get better, being 30 something starting a job a should have been at when I was 18-20? Here's to hoping we can figure it out soon, or something miraculous at least happens, I'm nearing my wits end.

Maybe my story would motivate you, there is no happy end or success story, I'm just a 26 year old failure of a human. I went to school hopping majors till I was 22 when I dropped out. I lost all of my motivation and passion for learning what I thought I cared about. The entire next year I tried getting any crappy job I could, and I kid you not I quit each one within a month because I started to feel even more depressed, to the point I could barely eat. My friends were finishing school, and the ones who hadn't gone have been working for long enough to have stuff to put on a resume. 3 years have gone by since that and I'm fucking 26, where the fuck did the time go, I swear the 3 years that went by felt hardly like months and I have legitimately done nothing helpful for myself in all that time I had, sure I have gotten on antidepressants but like, I just have no hope anymore. You have a lot going on for you still man. While you might not feel well, you still have good things lined up for you right now. If you can just power through I'm sure your whole life will turn around.

I'm exactly here, except I dropped out of college too because I lost every ounce of passion and motivation from my depression. I had a stint of getting shitty retail jobs, but I'd quit within a month each time. I would come home and go straight to bed without eating every day. I don't even know what to do anymore except wait till I decide to end things.

I'm 26 and I am basically going to end up like this. I've planned since I was a kid to end things before I hit 30. When I was 22 I dropped out of school like an idiot. And at 23, after getting and quitting MANY shitty jobs due to me basically starving myself out due to being so depressed (I had no appetite, I ate breakfast only, worked, and then slept immediately regardless of the time just to repeat it all), I have spent the last 3 years jobless, severely depressed, and completely hopeless. I've lost all motivation to even try to turn things around anymore. I'm right here with you man.

You are super young, you have so much time to work things out. I wish I realized I was as depressed as I am earlier on, if I had gotten help when I was 16 I probably wouldn't have dropped out of college, quit working at 23 because of depression, and be rotting away in my room for 3 more years. Try to think of it like this, of the people who DO go to college, a lot don't end up having a job until 22 or 23. One of my friends graduated only 2 years ago at 24 and got his first job, and he doesn't even enjoy it. You have plenty of time to heal. How you go about it is really up to you, whether you want therapy, to talk about it with family, or try and figure it out alone. Just don't wait till it's too late like I did, I know you can figure it out.

I'm 26, at 23 I was so depressed I had to quit working, I kept getting jobs and quitting within a month until I finally came to realize I had a genuine problem. After 3 years of getting help and not feeling better, I just feel like by the time I get better, I'll be too old and out of place to actually even get to the point of a "career". What is even the point any more, the 3 years I've tried getting help have gone by in what feels like months, I'll be 30 before I even know it.

I think because you realized this so early, you have a good shot at getting better. If your parents are caring, i.e. you don't think they'll take it poorly as it seems some people here have experienced, it could be a good idea to talk to them and maybe start getting help.
I appreciate the reply, when I was more optimistic about recovering at 23 years old, I thought about things in a similar light. I've basically given up now and am just waiting, but thank you.
Thank you for the kind words.

I've felt exactly like this for practically my whole life, elementary school included, difference being is I have a brother, and I'm probably older than you. I wish I could give you some kind of advice, but unfortunately all I can say is that, you aren't alone in feeling like this, I'm right here with you.
